currentContext.strategies: Localisation and vertical integration remain central to strategy, reducing import dependence and strengthening domestic supply chains.|Continue to invest in expanding manufacturing capacity through state-of-the-art facilities that will support next-generation customer programmes while enhancing productivity and operational agility.|Technology leadership anchored in the long-standing Stanley Electric partnership combined with engineering capability across India, Taiwan and the Czech Republic.|Strategic emphasis on technology-driven products aligned with future mobility trends -- LED platforms, smart lighting applications and emerging technologies catering to EVs and next-generation vehicles.|Digital transformation agenda: strengthening cybersecurity, accelerating AI adoption (Google Workspace upgraded to Enterprise with Gemini), Manufacturing Execution System (MES) implemented at the Bawal SMT Electronics plant, and the 3DEXPERIENCE PLM platform to digitally manage the product lifecycle.|Continued focus on enhancing manufacturing efficiency, localisation and supply-chain resilience in response to global geopolitical uncertainty, commodity price volatility and changing sourcing patterns.
currentContext.expansion: Lumax commercialised Chakan (Pune) Phase 2 in FY 2025-26, adding highly automated capacity for advanced LED assemblies serving premium SUV and new-platform rollouts from Pune's OEM cluster (Tata Motors, SAVW). Sanand 2, Gujarat was operationalised in Q1 FY 2025-26, positioned in Gujarat's western automotive corridor to serve Maruti Suzuki's Sanand operations and other Gujarat OEMs. A new greenfield plant at Bengaluru, Karnataka was board-approved in Q2 FY 2025-26 (capital outlay Rs 140 Crore) and is to be commissioned by Q4 FY 2026-27, catering to new orders from MSIL and Toyota Kirloskar Motor and marking Lumax's entry into India's southern automotive manufacturing hub -- this is also referenced elsewhere in the report as the new plant being set up at Bidadi Industrial Area, Bengaluru. Separately, during the year the Company invested Rs 40,825.75 Lakhs towards capacity expansion of its manufacturing facilities and Rs 1,609.04 Lakhs on R&D facilities at Chakan and Gurugram. The FY 2025-26 capex cycle (Rs 350-400 Crore, above original guidance) was deliberately front-loaded and funded through internal accruals rather than debt; FY 2026-27 capex is planned to moderate to Rs 100-150 Crore as the Company shifts from building capacity to harvesting it. On localisation, the Company has achieved 30-35% overall localisation of LED electronic components, with PCBs reaching 70% localisation at the dedicated electronics facility in Bawal, Haryana (developed as part of the extended Stanley Electric JV); further localisation of LED driver modules is the next planned step. Lumax is also expanding into HVAC control panels and interior electronics as a second growth engine, built on the same lighting-derived capabilities (electronics design, PCB manufacturing, plastic moulding, mechatronics) and manufactured at Bawal under the extended Stanley Electric partnership, with commercial orders being received. In advanced technology, Lumax developed Adaptive Driving Beam (ADB) technology and sequential turn indicators, showcased an ADB headlamp for two-wheelers at iSOL 2025, and is targeting its first commercial ADB application.

risks.note: Top 3 OEM customers represent approximately 61% of FY 2025-26 revenues; pricing actions or volume reductions by any one customer could materially impact performance.
Despite 30-35% overall localisation, significant LED driver module imports create exposure to tariff escalation and currency depreciation.
US tariff escalation, Red Sea freight disruptions, and West Asia crude price elevation create both direct cost pressures and indirect demand impacts.
Rising crude oil prices impact polymer and plastics input costs, which are significant raw materials in lamp housing and moulding.
EV penetration curves can be non-linear; slower-than-expected adoption extends the payback period on EV-specific design investments.
Rapid change in lighting technology (OLED, micro-LED, laser) could displace conventional LED if Lumax is not at the frontier.
Global Tier-1 suppliers and new domestic entrants compete for premium OEM platform design-ins as India's lighting market consolidates.
Evolving automotive safety, emissions and cybersecurity standards (e.g. Bharat NCAP 2.0, AIS-008/012, AIS-189/190) require continuous compliance investment and product adaptation.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

It operates 12 manufacturing facilities across Haryana, Uttarakhand, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, supported by R&D centres in Gurugram and Pune and overseas design centres in Taiwan and the Czech Republic.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Expansion into TVS, Suzuki, Yamaha 2W; entry into Toyota Kirloskar (first headlamp win); HVAC business operational (Rs.35-40cr annual revenue); potential localization of LED modules (current 25%-30%, target 50%-60%)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural shift towards LED lighting adoption is increasing lighting content and value per vehicle.
- Premiumisation across vehicle segments and growing SUV preference are driving higher-value platform wins.
- GST 2.0 reforms (effective September 22, 2025) provided a significant demand tailwind for the automotive sector.
- Two-wheeler segment recovery supported by rural consumption and rising demand for premium and electric mobility solutions.
- LED revenue share moved from 58% to 61% this year, with the current order book at 88% LED -- the mix shift is expected to accelerate.
- Localisation (PCB bare boards at 60-70%, connectors at 35-40%) is reducing import dependence and insulating margins from currency and freight cost volatility.
- India's economy remained resilient (RBI-estimated real GDP growth of 7.6% in FY26) supporting overall auto demand, though industry growth moderated due to inflationary pressures, evolving consumer spending patterns, supply chain realignments and heightened competition.
- Management remains cautiously optimistic on the medium-to-long-term outlook for the Indian automotive industry, citing continued infrastructure development, increasing vehicle electrification, rising safety awareness and policy support for domestic manufacturing.
- Robust order book cited as providing strong visibility for future growth.
- LED lighting products now form a significant part of the order pipeline, reflecting the industry-wide transition toward energy-efficient, high-value lighting systems.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin 9% in Q2 (ex-FX: 9.7%-9.8%); raw material cost ~64%-65%; manpower cost ~12.5% (target 11%-11.5%); other fixed costs ~14%-15% (target 12%-13%); margin expansion via operating leverage, localization, and content per vehicle growth

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing capex for order book fulfillment (Bengaluru, Chakan); no dividends or buybacks mentioned; debt reduction via internal accruals; L/E ratio at 0.44

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Lumax commercialised Chakan (Pune) Phase 2 in FY 2025-26, adding highly automated capacity for advanced LED assemblies serving premium SUV and new-platform rollouts from Pune's OEM cluster (Tata Motors, SAVW). Sanand 2, Gujarat was operationalised in Q1 FY 2025-26, positioned in Gujarat's western automotive corridor to serve Maruti Suzuki's Sanand operations and other Gujarat OEMs. A new greenfield plant at Bengaluru, Karnataka was board-approved in Q2 FY 2025-26 (capital outlay Rs 140 Crore) and is to be commissioned by Q4 FY 2026-27, catering to new orders from MSIL and Toyota Kirloskar Motor and marking Lumax's entry into India's southern automotive manufacturing hub -- this is also referenced elsewhere in the report as the new plant being set up at Bidadi Industrial Area, Bengaluru. Separately, during the year the Company invested Rs 40,825.75 Lakhs towards capacity expansion of its manufacturing facilities and Rs 1,609.04 Lakhs on R&D facilities at Chakan and Gurugram. The FY 2025-26 capex cycle (Rs 350-400 Crore, above original guidance) was deliberately front-loaded and funded through internal accruals rather than debt; FY 2026-27 capex is planned to moderate to Rs 100-150 Crore as the Company shifts from building capacity to harvesting it. On localisation, the Company has achieved 30-35% overall localisation of LED electronic components, with PCBs reaching 70% localisation at the dedicated electronics facility in Bawal, Haryana (developed as part of the extended Stanley Electric JV); further localisation of LED driver modules is the next planned step. Lumax is also expanding into HVAC control panels and interior electronics as a second growth engine, built on the same lighting-derived capabilities (electronics design, PCB manufacturing, plastic moulding, mechatronics) and manufactured at Bawal under the extended Stanley Electric partnership, with commercial orders being received. In advanced technology, Lumax developed Adaptive Driving Beam (ADB) technology and sequential turn indicators, showcased an ADB headlamp for two-wheelers at iSOL 2025, and is targeting its first commercial ADB application.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, forward-looking, tech-driven; emphasized engineering superiority, localization roadmap, and margin expansion over 2-3 years; dismissed EV hype (only 9% order book), focused on LED and content growth

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Market leadership (#1) in Indian automotive lighting, positioned as a Tier 0.5 supplier to every major OEM
- Four-decade technology partnership with Stanley Electric Co. Ltd, Japan (37.5% equity stake in LIL), spanning lighting design, electronics integration and PCB manufacturing
- Nearly three-decade association with SL Corporation, South Korea, covering end-to-end lighting systems and automotive components
- One of very few Indian players offering a fully integrated, in-house designed/developed/manufactured LED, conventional lighting and electronics portfolio
- Long-standing OEM relationships built on trust and responsive engineering support (Maruti Suzuki, Hero MotoCorp, Honda, Mahindra & Mahindra, Tata Motors, Toyota, TVS, Royal Enfield, Ashok Leyland)
- Proximity to customers via 12 manufacturing facilities across major Indian auto hubs, enabling rapid-response engineering support and supply reliability

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: FX volatility (25%-30% USD imports); customer concentration (top 5 = 79% revenue); competitive intensity in lighting; LED module localization delays; Hyundai JV (SL Lumax) under pressure due to weak Hyundai sales

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Bengaluru plant is not just for volume — it’s strategically positioned to serve Toyota and Maruti’s export-bound eVitara, which could generate Rs.400-500cr/year; SL Lumax’s underperformance is tied to Hyundai’s sales slump, not Lumax’s execution

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Group structure] SL Lumax Limited is a separate JV entity (Lumax holds 21.28%) whose Rs. 2,933 Crore FY26 revenue is disclosed alongside — but is not part of — Lumax Industries' own Rs. 4,184 Crore FY26 revenue; consolidated PAT includes a 'Profit of Associate' line.
- [Corporate history] A demerger of Lumax Industries is recorded in the 2003 milestone, with no further detail given.
- [Leadership] Board includes three Stanley Electric nominee directors (Mr. Tadayoshi Aoki, Mr. Kenjiro Nakazono, Mr. Tomohiro Kondo); Mr. Deepak Jain is Chairman & Managing Director and Mr. Anmol Jain Joint Managing Director, with Mr. Dhanesh Kumar Jain as Chairman Emeritus.
- [External environment] Management flags "geopolitical challenges including supply chain disruptions and volatility in input costs" while claiming earnings growth exceeded revenue expansion.
- [Recognition] Awards cited include Maruti Suzuki Vendor Conference 2026 for sustainability, Tata Motors Sustainability Excellence Award 2025, CII-ITC Sustainability Award (Dharuhera), GreenPro Ecolabel certification for five products each from Bawal, Dharuhera, Haridwar, Pantnagar and Sanand, and LACP ranking #61 globally for its Integrated Annual Report.
